Now I have all 8 views. Let me analyze:

**Test image key features:**
- Hand holding soybean leaf showing the underside
- Possible grayish/whitish material visible on the underside of the held leaf
- Background leaves show scattered small yellow spots
- A few reddish-brown lesions visible in background

**Comparison summary:**
- **Downy_mildew** (view 1): Best match - very similar setup (hand holding leaf to show underside), small yellow-green spots on background leaves. Downy mildew's key feature is tan/gray fungal tufts on underside, matching the whitish texture on the held leaf
- **Soybean_rust**: Many dense reddish-brown spots - too many small spots compared to test image
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery circular patches - clearly different pattern
- **Bacterial_Pustule**: Small scattered reddish spots - doesn't match the yellow spot pattern
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Circular gray-centered lesions with red borders - different pattern
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Heavily yellowed leaves with dark spots - doesn't match (leaves still green)
- **Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus**: Irregular larger yellow-brown lesions along veins - some similarity but spots not vein-associated
- **Cercospora**: Dense reddish-purple discoloration - clearly different

The Downy_mildew reference (Soybean_Dise_11) was nearly identical in composition to the test image - hand holding leaf showing underside with small yellow-green spots on surrounding leaves. The whitish texture on the underside of the held leaf aligns with the characteristic tan/gray fungal tufts of downy mildew.
